sections.Interpretation: Severe microcytic hypochromic anaemia is present, with haemoglobin 6.2 g/dL, haematocrit 22.1% and red cell count 3.56 x10^12/L. The low mean cell volume and mean cell haemoglobin, together with the raised red cell distribution width, indicate marked anisocytosis and a pattern consistent with iron deficiency. A reactive thrombocytosis at 480 x10^9/L is in keeping with iron deficiency and ongoing blood loss. The white cell count and differential are within normal limits. The history of menorrhagia makes chronic blood loss the most likely cause, and iron studies and a reticulocyte count are recommended to confirm the diagnosis.
sections.Comment/recommendation: CRITICAL VALUE: Haemoglobin 6.2 g/dL is a critical result. Recommend urgent clinical review of this patient, including assessment of haemodynamic status and the need for transfusion. Urgent iron studies (serum ferritin, serum iron, transferrin saturation and total iron-binding capacity) and a reticulocyte count should be sent, and the source of menstrual blood loss should be investigated.
